title: Avo-4-part-3
description: Comprehensive exam covering EWIS, aircraft wiring, electrical buses, inverters, connectors, splicing, grounding, and electrical protection.

questions.question: What does EWIS represent
questions.explanation: EWIS stands for Electrical Wiring Interconnection System and covers the aircraft wiring and associated interconnections.

questions.question: ___ are caused by friction between two surfaces of different materials, at least one of which is conductive
questions.explanation: Electrostatic charges can be produced by friction between dissimilar materials when at least one material is conductive.

questions.question: Which of the following operates in conductive liquid
questions.explanation: A tilt switch is a device that responds to changes in orientation and can operate in or with conductive liquid applications.

questions.question: ___ are devices attached to the ends of cables and wires to make them easier to connect and disconnect
questions.explanation: Connectors are fitted to cable and wire ends to allow electrical circuits to be connected and disconnected efficiently.

questions.question: Purpose of wire splicing in A/C
options: B. Connect two or more wires securely
questions.explanation: Wire splicing provides a secure electrical and mechanical connection between two or more wires.

questions.question: Proper check of wire
questions.explanation: A digital multimeter can be used for common electrical checks such as voltage, resistance, and continuity.

questions.question: Which of the f/f is not the adv. of slack installation
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Prevent mechanical twisting. Slack in an installation provides flexibility and helps accommodate movement without transmitting excessive mechanical stress to the wiring.

questions.question: ___ is used to connect two A/C metallic component to form an integrate unit
questions.explanation: Bonding electrically connects metallic aircraft components so they form an integrated electrical unit and maintain an effective electrical path.

questions.question: Type of transformer used in TRU
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Step down. A transformer in a TRU reduces the AC voltage to the level required before rectification.

questions.question: Split-parallel bus system during normal flight, all four engine driven generators operating in
questions.explanation: In the stated normal operating condition, the engine-driven generators operate in parallel so their power can be shared through the common distribution arrangement.

questions.question: Which of the following power services is used to ensure safe flight during an emergency situation
questions.explanation: Essential services are electrical services required to support safe aircraft operation during an emergency.

questions.question: What would designate a wire printed with the number M22719/34-22-948 the number 22
questions.explanation: In the designation M22719/34-22-948, the number 22 identifies the wire size according to the applicable wire specification.

questions.question: Bus commonly used to denote
options: A. Essential AC bus, left DC, battery
C. Generator bus, standby bus, ground
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the bus designation as Essential AC bus, left DC, battery, which refers to important aircraft electrical distribution buses.

questions.question: ___ allows current to flow from AC to DC power only
questions.explanation: A rectifier allows electrical power to be converted from AC to DC by permitting the required one-way current flow.

questions.question: Not true about intermittent load
options: A. Ammeter may exceed redline continuously
B. Intermittent loads never require current limits
C. Ammeter should never exceed redline in intermittent duty
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Ammeter should never exceed redline in intermittent duty. Ammeter indications and operating limits must remain within the applicable instrument limits.

questions.question: Use to make or break electrical contact
questions.explanation: A switch is used to make or break an electrical circuit by opening or closing its contacts.

questions.question: Automatic switch used for protection from overload or short circuit
questions.explanation: A circuit breaker automatically opens a circuit when excessive current caused by an overload or short circuit is detected.

questions.question: Attaching one metal to another by melting
questions.explanation: Soldering joins conductors or metal parts by melting solder to form an electrical and mechanical joint.

questions.question: ___ gives mechanical strength
questions.explanation: Conduits provide mechanical protection and support for wires and cables routed through aircraft structure.

questions.question: DC motor drive 3 phase AC generator
questions.explanation: A rotary inverter uses a DC motor to mechanically drive an AC generator, producing AC power from a DC source.

questions.question: Throw indicate in SPST
questions.explanation: In an SPST switch, the throw describes the path or circuit connection that is made or broken by the switch.

questions.question: Before crimping stripping
questions.explanation: Before crimping a terminal onto a wire, the insulation must be stripped to expose the conductor for the proper connection.

questions.question: On device symbol identification for the item damaged by ESD
questions.explanation: ESD-susceptible devices can be damaged by electrostatic discharge and therefore require appropriate handling and protection.

questions.question: For large aircraft for emergency AC power
questions.explanation: A static inverter provides emergency AC power from a DC source without using rotating mechanical machinery.

questions.question: Fuses are connected in
questions.explanation: Fuses are connected in series so that excessive current passes through the fuse element and causes it to open the circuit.

questions.question: In parallel electrical system, all A.C generator are connected to one distribution bus is
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Essential bus system. An aircraft bus system distributes electrical power to groups of electrical loads according to their operational importance.

questions.question: In a parallel electrical system, all A.C generator are connected to one distribution bus is called
questions.explanation: A split-parallel bus (tie-bus) arrangement allows generators and buses to be interconnected or separated according to the aircraft electrical configuration.

questions.question: On both rotary and static inverters the input power is
questions.explanation: Rotary and static inverters receive DC input power and convert it to AC output power.

questions.question: If the wiring size is 24 AWG what will be the sleeving size
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is 12. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: Which of the following is not the main purpose of the separation routing rules of wire cable
options: C. To increase the strength of the cable
questions.explanation: Separation and routing rules are intended to prevent interference, damage, and common-cause failures; increasing cable strength is not their primary purpose.

questions.question: Wires are usually joined at
questions.explanation: Terminal strips provide organized points where aircraft wires can be joined, distributed, and terminated.

questions.question: Single pole single throw, throw indicates
questions.explanation: In SPST terminology, the throw identifies the electrical path selected or controlled by the switch.

questions.question: ___ is source, which convert unregulated DC to regulated DC
questions.explanation: A converter changes unregulated DC into regulated DC so that the supplied equipment receives a controlled DC voltage.

questions.question: How can cable & wire is identified
questions.explanation: Aircraft wires and cables can be identified using direct markings or indirect identification methods such as identification sleeves.

questions.question: Identification marking sleeve should be placed at each end of wire and at
options: B. 15-inch maximum intervals along the wire
questions.explanation: Identification sleeves are placed at wire ends and at specified intervals along long wire runs so the wiring remains identifiable.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an intermittent load
options: C. Landing gear, flaps, trim motor, landing light
questions.explanation: Landing gear, flaps, trim motors, and landing lights are examples of loads that operate for limited periods rather than continuously.

questions.question: What is intermittent load
options: A. Operated for two minutes or less and are the
C. Operated only during engine shutdown
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Operated for two minutes or less and are the. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: What is the difficulty in connecting AC power generators in parallel
options: A. Matching wire sizes is required
B. Synchronization of frequency, voltage and phase is required
questions.explanation: AC generators must be synchronized in frequency, voltage, and phase before being connected in parallel.

questions.question: Not EFIS troubleshooting used
questions.explanation: Splicing is a wiring repair or connection technique, not an EFIS troubleshooting method.

questions.question: Not true about splicing
options: B. Insulated conductors are always prohibited
C. Splices must always be soldered
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Non-insulated is appropriate. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: ESD mat is used to
questions.explanation: An ESD mat provides a controlled path for dissipating electrostatic charges and helps protect sensitive electronic components.

questions.question: Not used to bundle wires
questions.explanation: Clamps are commonly used to support and secure wire bundles; brazing is a joining process rather than a normal wire-bundling method.

questions.question: ___ are connected directly to the battery bus
questions.explanation: Vital services are connected directly or preferentially to the battery bus so that important loads can remain powered when normal generation is unavailable.

questions.question: ___ used for checking insulation leakage
questions.explanation: A Megger test is used to measure insulation resistance and detect insulation leakage or deterioration.

questions.question: Load shedding in the event of overload ___ reduce electricity to acceptable level
questions.explanation: The BPCU, or bus power control function, controls electrical distribution and can shed selected loads during overload conditions.

questions.question: Parallel electrical system all AC generator connected to one distribution
questions.explanation: A tie bus provides a connection between electrical bus sections and can allow generators to supply a common distribution arrangement.

questions.question: Prior to soldering used to prepare the surface of the conductor
questions.explanation: Flux is applied during soldering to prepare and clean the conductor surface and promote proper solder wetting.

questions.question: Current carrying capacity parameter
options: A. Color, insulation age, connector type
questions.explanation: Current-carrying capacity depends on factors such as conductor length, conductor area, and the ability to dissipate heat.

questions.question: Solderability affected by two alloys
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Magnesium and silicon. These alloying elements can influence the properties and solderability of aluminum materials.

questions.question: To protect aircraft & person from damage by lighting discharge
questions.explanation: Grounding the aircraft provides a controlled electrical path and helps protect the aircraft and personnel from lightning and other electrical discharge effects.

questions.question: True about rotary inverter
options: A. DC motor drives a three-phase AC generator
B. Transformer converts DC directly to AC
C. DC motor drive 3-phase AC generator
questions.explanation: A rotary inverter consists of a DC motor mechanically driving a three-phase AC generator.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a wire connector in aircraft EWIS
options: A. To facilitate easy removal & replacement of components
questions.explanation: Aircraft wire connectors make it easier to disconnect and replace components without disturbing the entire wiring installation.

questions.question: ___ is approved for splicing individual wires in a group of bundle
questions.explanation: Individual wire splices within a bundle require the applicable engineering approval and approved maintenance procedures.

questions.question: Crimping handle is
questions.explanation: Crimping tools are commonly color coded so the correct die or terminal range can be identified and used.

questions.question: Which of the following is true
options: A. Crimping connections are stronger, actually as strong as the conductor itself
questions.explanation: Properly made crimping connections can provide a strong, reliable electrical and mechanical connection comparable to the conductor itself.

questions.question: ___ is a process of joining two pieces of base metals by creating metallic joint
questions.explanation: Brazing joins base metals by heating the joint and melting a filler metal without melting the base metals themselves.

questions.question: The main bus galley bus receive their power from the
questions.explanation: The AC transfer bus is a distribution point from which specified aircraft AC loads, including the main and galley buses in the stated arrangement, receive power.

questions.question: Buses are commonly used to denote essential
options: A. AC bus, left DC bus, battery
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is AC bus, left DC bus, battery. These are common designations used to identify important aircraft electrical buses.

questions.question: In TRU the transformer is
questions.explanation: The transformer in a TRU is a step-down transformer because the incoming AC voltage must be reduced before rectification to DC.

questions.question: For emergency DC power, it is supplied by the
questions.explanation: The vital DC bus supplies essential DC loads when normal electrical generation is unavailable or during an emergency configuration.

questions.question: The current rating of a cable of wire indicates the
options: A. Current capacity that the wire or cables can safely carry continuously
questions.explanation: Current rating indicates the current capacity that the wire or cable can safely carry continuously under specified conditions.

questions.question: Power-consuming devices are always supplied from bus
questions.explanation: Vital DC consumers are connected to the appropriate vital DC distribution so essential equipment can remain powered during emergency conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following wire has the largest wire size
questions.explanation: In the AWG system, a smaller gauge number represents a larger conductor; 0000 AWG is therefore a very large wire size.

questions.question: Wire conduit kinked should be
questions.explanation: A kinked conduit can damage or excessively stress the wiring, so the damaged conduit should be replaced according to approved maintenance procedures.

questions.question: Minimum bending radius of bends in wire group is
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is 10 times. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: ___ are devices attached to the ends of cables and sets of wires to make them easier to connect and disconnect
questions.explanation: Connectors are attached to cable and wire ends to provide convenient and secure electrical connections and allow disconnection when required.

questions.question: What is primary purpose of conduit
options: A. Mechanical protection for cables and wires
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of conduit is to provide mechanical protection to wires and cables against damage from the surrounding aircraft structure and environment.

questions.question: Electro-mechanical switch
questions.explanation: A relay is an electromechanical switch that uses an electrically controlled coil to open or close another circuit.

questions.question: Which of the following consumer device are supplied w/ power when twin engine operated aircraft both generators are operating
questions.explanation: When both generators are operating normally on a twin-engine aircraft, the electrical system can supply the aircraft's consumer devices according to its distribution configuration.

questions.question: What is purpose of wire splicing in EWIS
questions.explanation: Wire splicing is used for connecting broken or separated wires while maintaining an approved electrical and mechanical connection.

questions.question: Aircraft critical component is operated by
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Aircraft battery. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: Which device is denoted
questions.explanation: A switch is an electrical device used to open or close a circuit and control the flow of current.

questions.question: Aluminum wire size should be selected on basis of
questions.explanation: Aluminum wire size is selected primarily according to the required current-carrying capacity and applicable installation conditions.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not used to test wire
questions.explanation: An oscilloscope is useful for observing electrical waveforms, but it is not the normal primary instrument for basic aircraft wire testing such as continuity and insulation checks.

questions.question: One of the following is not component of EWIS
questions.explanation: An LRU is a replaceable aircraft equipment unit rather than a component of the EWIS itself.

questions.question: Service used for safe flight during emergency
questions.explanation: Essential services are the services that must remain available to support safe flight and landing during an emergency.

questions.question: Not factor for determining wire size
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Insulation strength. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: Input for inverter
questions.explanation: An inverter normally receives DC power, such as from the aircraft DC battery or DC bus, and converts it to AC.

questions.question: Which type of cable does antenna's use
questions.explanation: Coaxial cable is commonly used for antenna circuits because its construction provides controlled impedance and shielding.

questions.question: ___ services are those which can be isolated in flight emergency
questions.explanation: Non-essential services are loads that can be disconnected or isolated during an emergency to preserve power for essential functions.

questions.question: During the failure of both engines, the power source which feeds essential load is
questions.explanation: An inverter can provide AC power from the aircraft DC system when normal AC generation is unavailable, such as during an emergency.

questions.question: Most critical systems required for safe landing in the case of emergency
questions.explanation: Navigation and communication systems are among the critical systems that may be required to support safe landing during an emergency.

questions.question: Inverter is used for
questions.explanation: An inverter is used in an emergency situation when AC power is required from an available DC source.

questions.question: The output of inverter is
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is 115V and 400Hz. This is the specified AC output associated with the inverter in the source material.

questions.question: A/C battery power distribution method of modern aircraft with twin generator
questions.explanation: A split-bus arrangement is used on many twin-generator aircraft so the electrical distribution can be separated or interconnected as required.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an intermittent load
options: B. Landing gear, flaps, trim motor, landing light
questions.explanation: Landing gear, flaps, trim motors, and landing lights are typical intermittent loads because they are generally operated for limited periods.

questions.question: In the event of system overload, the control unit must reduce the electrical load to an acceptable level. This is known as
questions.explanation: Load shedding is the deliberate removal of selected electrical loads to reduce total demand to an acceptable level during an overload.

questions.question: ___ are used in almost all electrical systems with the exception of firefighting and firewarning systems
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Normal cables. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: ___ are stronger, actually as strong as the conductor itself
questions.explanation: Crimping connections can produce a strong electrical and mechanical joint when the correct terminal, wire, and approved crimping procedure are used.

questions.question: Electrical power is applied to various electrically energized components in an aircraft via a common point called
questions.explanation: A busbar or bus provides a common electrical distribution point from which multiple electrically powered components can receive power.

questions.question: Critical component gets power from
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is Battery. The answer is retained exactly as supplied in the source.

questions.question: In a single solid rod of filament drawn metals enclosed in suitable insulating material and outer protective material
questions.explanation: A wire is a conductor made from metal filament or strands enclosed by suitable insulating and protective material.

questions.question: ___ are electronic components and other parts that are prone to damage from stray electric charge
questions.explanation: An electrostatic sensitive device is an electronic component or assembly that can be damaged by stray electrostatic charge.
